benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, triangulated from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official residential points (Tochidai/Tochinokati): Funabashi and Keisei-Funabashi ~105, Tsudanuma (Funabashi side) ~115, Nishi-Funabashi ~95, Shimosa-Nakayama ~95, Higashi-Nakayama ~95, Kaijin ~94, Daijingushita ~90 (thin), Higashi-Kaijin ~90 (proxy), Shin-Funabashi ~87, Higashi-Funabashi ~85, Baraki-Nakayama ~85 (proxy), Funabashi-Keibajo ~88 (thin), then the northern plateau branch lines: Maehara ~70, Tsukada ~65, Kita-Narashino ~60 (proxy), Takane-Kido ~60, Yakuen-dai ~53, Funabashi-Hoten ~50, Funabashi-Nichidaimae ~50, Hasama ~45, Futawa-Mukodai ~42, Magomezawa ~40 (proxy), Takane-Kodan ~36, Misaki ~30, Takifudo ~30. Tochidai's headline station totals pool official points up to 3 km away in cheaper districts and are not used where they drag (Takane-Kido's raw 48.7 is pulled down by Matsugaoka points outside the walk zone; its in-zone points average 60.4). Stations marked proxy rest on official points or neighbouring-station figures, flagged as such. Walk bands apply the observed gradient: land falls ~30–35% by a 10-minute walk at the major stations (~45% by 15 minutes) and ~13–20% by 10 minutes on the branch lines. Used houses transacted at about ¥112万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): Higashi-Nakayama/Minatomachi ~150, the Natsumi/Narashinodai plateau ~130–140, Fujiwara ~119, Takinoi ~84; 30+-year stock runs at roughly 45–50% of under-10-year stock per tsubo. Official residential land prices rose +4.5% in the 2026 prefectural survey after +5.3% in 2025.
